title: Explain the course once
statement: Explain how a course works once, at first open, with a help entry to return to it, instead of re-explaining the machinery at the start of every unit.
detail: The review of a Grade 9 prototype found each unit's opening doing two jobs, re-explaining how the program works and introducing the text, made explaining the program once, at first open, a P1 build item, and asked for a help entry as a way back for a student who joins mid-year or returns after a gap (`g9/library/text/L36b8ba.txt`, lines 57-58). Its note argues that every second spent re-explaining the machinery from unit two onward is a second not spent on the text, and a recurring source of the sense that the lesson is long (line 140).
against: The reason given, that re-explaining the machinery takes time from the text and makes the lesson feel long, is a review note, which the review offers as rationale that has not been confirmed (`g9/library/text/L36b8ba.txt`, line 13).

evidence.quote: Explain the program once, at first open. Remove the per-unit re-explanation of how the program works.
Provide a way back to that explanation for a student who joins mid-year or returns after a gap — a help entry, not a repeated beat.

Every second spent re-explaining the machinery in unit two onward is a second not spent on the text, and it removes a recurring source of the sensation that the lesson is long — the opening of each unit currently has to do two jobs.
